# Weezer's Voyage to the Blue Planet: The Concert Film

## Lead Section

**Weezer's Voyage to the Blue Planet: The Concert Film** is a 2024 documentary-music film directed by Garrett Nicholson that captures American rock band Weezer's **Voyage to the Blue Planet Tour**, celebrating the 30th anniversary of their 1994 self-titled debut album, commonly known as "The Blue Album" . The film was recorded at Boston's TD Garden on September 10, 2024, and was released for digital streaming on October 13-14, 2024 . It features the band performing their classic album in its entirety alongside other hits, presented within a science fiction narrative framework .

## Background and Production

### Concept and Development

The film emerged from Weezer's 2024 North American tour of the same name, which ran from September 4 to October 12, 2024 . The tour was conceived to celebrate the 30th anniversary of "The Blue Album," which has been listed in Rolling Stone's "500 Greatest Albums of All Time" . The concert film concept was announced on September 27, 2024, with band members Rivers Cuomo, Brian Bell, Patrick Wilson, and Scott Shriner describing it as "one small step for man, one giant leap for Weezerkind" .

The film was produced by Mike Holland through Moment.co , with Garrett Nicholson serving as director, cinematographer, and editor . Karl Koch also contributed as a cinematographer . The production had an estimated budget of \$15 and was shot in color with a 16:9 HD aspect ratio .

### Recording and Release

The concert footage was captured during Weezer's performance at TD Garden in Boston on September 10, 2024 . The film was released for digital streaming and on-demand viewing starting October 13, 2024 . It was made available through various platforms, allowing fans who couldn't attend the live tour to experience the show .

## Film Content and Structure

### Storyline and Visual Elements

The film presents a science fiction narrative that serves as a framework for the concert performance. The storyline begins with a breaking news report informing the audience that the Blue Planet is dying, and Weezer has been sent to restore it . The band boards the "Betsy 2.0" shuttle, taking the audience on a dangerous voyage through space .

As the band performs, the screen shows the shuttle flying through space, traveling through a Weezer-themed space bar, and encountering an alien named Bokkus who harbors hatred for the group . During the journey, they pass through the "Pinkerton Asteroid Belt," where Bokkus attacks the shuttle by hurling pies and other objects, draining its shields . The shuttle crashes, launching the band members onto the surface of the Blue Planet .

Upon arrival, they discover the planet is gray and dying. Rivers Cuomo plants a flag adorned with the band's "Flying =W=" symbol in the ground, declaring: "That's one small step for Weezer, one giant leap for Weezerkind" . The band then performs the entire Blue Album front-to-back, which revives the planet, causing grass, trees, and buildings to grow as they play .

### Musical Performance

The film features Weezer performing a setlist that includes songs from multiple albums, structured around three parts: the **Blue Voyage Takeoff**, the **Pinkerton Asteroid Belt**, and the **Blue Planet** . The Blue Voyage Takeoff section includes high-energy hits like "Hash Pipe," "Beverly Hills," "Dope Nose," "Pork and Beans," and "Island in the Sun" .

The Pinkerton Asteroid Belt segment features five songs from the band's 1996 album "Pinkerton," including "Getchoo," "Why Bother?," "Pink Triangle," "You Gave Your Love to Me Softly," and "Across the Sea" .

The final Blue Planet section consists of the entire Blue Album performed in sequence: "My Name is Jonas," "No One Else," "The World Has Turned and Left Me Here," "Buddy Holly," "Undone (The Sweater Song)," "Say It Ain't So," "In the Garage," and "Only in Dreams" .

### Stage Production

The film showcases elaborate stage production with a high-tech setup featuring a massive high-resolution video screen behind the band . The four musicians appear wearing blue astronaut suits at the beginning, and "launch" into their set as the screen shows their interstellar travel . Later in the show, Rivers Cuomo changes into a black-and-gold Star Trek-inspired uniform with the Weezer logo replacing the Starfleet insignia .

The production includes special effects such as fog, pyrotechnics, and confetti cannons that shoot blue streamers over the audience during key moments . The stage also features floating planets and rocks on the sides, creating a cosmic atmosphere that complements the space theme .

## Reception and Impact

### Critical Response

The film has received positive reception from audiences and critics alike. It has achieved a **100% audience score on TMDb** based on reviews from knowledgeable users . Critics have praised the production's elaborate stagecraft, calling it "one of the most compelling tours" they had ever seen . The show was described as "a feast for the eyes and ears" with terrific sound quality and a generous setlist .

Reviewers noted the film's unique blend of concert performance and science fiction narrative, describing it as "campy, nerdy, and for the entire 20,000-person arena, euphoric" . The production was particularly appreciated by families, with one reviewer noting that children especially enjoyed the story aspect of the show .

### Cultural Significance

The film represents a significant milestone in Weezer's career, commemorating three decades since the release of their breakthrough album. "The Blue Album" has had a lasting impact on alternative rock, and its inclusion in Rolling Stone's prestigious list underscores its cultural importance .

The **Voyage to the Blue Planet Tour** itself was notable for its family-friendly atmosphere, with many parents bringing their children to the shows. Reviewers observed that even young children knew the band's material well, suggesting the enduring appeal of Weezer's music across generations .

### Legacy

The concert film has been documented as part of Weezer's broader 30th anniversary celebration, which included special merchandise, fan club exclusives, and a one-off anniversary performance at Club Dump . The film's release allowed fans worldwide to experience the tour's elaborate production and narrative elements, extending the reach of the anniversary celebration beyond those who attended the live shows.

## Band Members

The film features Weezer's current lineup:

* **Rivers Cuomo** (lead vocals, lead guitar)

* **Patrick Wilson** (drums)

* **Brian Bell** (rhythm guitar, backing vocals, keyboards)

* **Scott Shriner** (bass, backing vocals)

1.title: “Grab your popcorn”: Weezer announce Voyage To The Blue Planet Tour concert film
1.content:
[Weezer](http://www.kerrang.com/artists/weezer) have announced a concert film for this year’s epic Voyage To The Blue Planet Tour.

Captured at Boston’s TD Garden on their huge anniversary run, the band will be releasing the movie on October 13 and 14 for fans to marvel over all the Blue Album bangers plus plenty of other hits – not to mention their awesome, out-of-this-world production in all its glory.

“One small step for man, one giant leap for Weezerkind,” announce Rivers Cuomo and co. “On October 13 + 14, we’re bringing you a very special concert film of The Voyage to the Blue Planet Tour (shot at the Boston show). For all of you that couldn’t make it out to the tour, now’s your chance to come celebrate 30 years of the Blue Album with us!

“Grab your popcorn and your early bird tickets.”

Watch the trailer now:

And catch Weezer on their remaining Voyage To The Blue Planet Tour dates:

September

27 Austin, TX Moody Center

28 Houston, TX Toyota Center

29 Dallas, TX American Airlines Center

October

1 Loveland, CO Blue FCU Arena

4 Seattle, WA Climate Pledge Arena

5 Vancouver, BC, Canada Rogers Arena

6 Portland, OR Moda Center

8 Sacramento, CA Golden 1 Center

9 San Francisco, CA Chase Center

11 Inglewood, CA Intuit Dome

7.title: WEEZER took Austin fans on a trip to their Blue Planet! | The Heart Sounds
7.description: Austin was treated to an epic night of rock as Weezer, Dinosaur Jr., and The Flaming Lips took the stage for an unforgettable show! Fans packed the Moody
7.content:
Austin, we have lift off!
-------------------------

Austin was treated to an epic night of rock as **Weezer**, **Dinosaur Jr.**, and **The Flaming Lips** took the stage for an unforgettable show! Fans packed the **Moody Center** with an electric energy, ready for a night of nostalgia and rock ‘n’ roll. With Weezer playing their iconic**_Blue Album_**in full, excitement was at an all-time high. Add the unique sounds of Dinosaur Jr. and the psychedelic energy of The Flaming Lips, and it was clear we were in for something special.

The lineup was a perfect blend of indie rock legends, making it a night to remember. From start to finish, the crowd was on their feet, singing along to every word, every riff, and every beat. It was a celebration of timeless music and a reminder of why these bands have stayed at the forefront of the rock scene for decades. We were there to bring you exclusive coverage, from epic live shots to an in-depth review.

![Image 1: Crowd of people gathers in a large venue, some taking pictures with their phones, while stage lights illuminate the arena](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza15.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

DINOSAUR JR.
------------

**Dinosaur Jr.** kicked off the night with an explosive set that reminded everyone why they’re considered pioneers of the alternative rock scene. **J Mascis’s** guitar work was nothing short of phenomenal, his fuzzy riffs and solos tearing through the Austin air. The band’s energy was raw and powerful, as they launched into hits like “Little Fury Things,” “Feel the Pain,” and “Freak Scene.”

Mascis’s laid-back yet intense presence, paired with **Lou Barlow’s** heavy bass and **Murph’s** pounding drums, created a wall of sound that had the crowd headbanging from the start.

Their blend of grunge and distortion-filled rock was a perfect way to set the tone for the night. The crowd responded with wild enthusiasm, feeding off the band’s energy. Each song felt like a journey, as Mascis’s guitar solos sent chills down the spine, while Barlow and Murph kept the rhythm tight and driving. Although their set was very short, around 25 minutes only, it was clear that Dinosaur Jr. still had that same fiery passion they did when they first exploded onto the scene. Their set was loud, raw, and filled with the kind of energy only true rock veterans can deliver. The perfect opening act to lead into the psychedelic wonder that was The Flaming Lips.

![Image 2: Dinosaur Jr. is performing live on stage, with the guitarist on the left, the drummer in the center, and the bass player on the right](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Dino-THS-01.jpg)

Dinosaur Jr - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 3: Guitarist, J. Mascis, is seen playing an electric guitar with guitar amplifiers stacked behind him](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Dino-THS-02.jpg)

Dinosaur Jr - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 4: A long-haired bassist wearing a Mister Rogers' Neighborhood T-shirt plays a glittery silver bass guitar on stage](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Dino-THS-03.jpg)

Dinosaur Jr - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

THE FLAMING LIPS
----------------

**The Flaming Lips** followed, transforming the stage into a surreal, psychedelic wonderland. **Wayne Coyne**, ever the showman, started his show even before their performance. The energy in the venue reached new heights as Coyne led the band into a mesmerizing performance filled with light shows, inflatable robots, and larger-than-life visuals. Tracks like “The Spark That Bled,” “Suddenly Everything Has Changed” and “She Don’t Use Jelly” had the crowd in a euphoric trance, with everyone singing along as neon lights and colorful balloons filled the air.

The Flaming Lips’ set was more than just music—it was a full sensory experience. Coyne’s emotional connection with the audience was evident as he thanked fans for their endless support, creating a sense of unity and joy. He even took the time to read all the names of the venues and shows they had ever played in Austin since the ‘80s! Their psychedelic rock sound paired perfectly with the visual spectacle they brought to the stage, making their set a vibrant, kaleidoscopic journey through sound and color.

They finished their set with the iconic song “Do You Realize” creating a magical and beautiful atmosphere inside the Moody Center. Every second felt like a celebration, and the crowd loved every second of it. The Flaming Lips delivered a performance that felt magical, leaving the audience in awe and perfectly primed for the night’s headliners—Weezer.

![Image 5: Wayne Coyne is holding a microphone in his left hand, singing live in front of an audience](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Flaming-THS-01.jpg)

The Flaming Lips - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 6: Musician wearing headphones and a striped shirt plays an electric guitar on stage](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Flaming-THS-02.jpg)

The Flaming Lips - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 7: Singer in a dark suit, with curly gray hair, singing passionately into a microphone on a stage bathed in blue and teal light, with laser beams adding to the atmosphere](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Flaming-THS-03.jpg)

The Flaming Lips - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 8: Musician playing on keyboard with two guitars nearby](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Flaming-THS-04.jpg)

The Flaming Lips - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 9: Man with curly gray hair, dressed in a suit and harness, singing into a microphone and holding a piece of paper, on a stage with blue lighting](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Flaming-THS-05.jpg)

The Flaming Lips - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 10: Maynard James Keenan is holding a long stick with a light on the end](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Flaming-THS-06.jpg)

The Flaming Lips - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 11: A man with curly hair holds a long stick with a lightbulb at the end, possibly on stage, in a black and white photograph](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Flaming-THS-07.jpg)

The Flaming Lips - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

WEEZER
------

Finally, it was time for Weezer, and the crowd erupted as the spaceship took off, leaving Rivers, Brian, Patrick, and Scott on the “Blue Planet.” The band wasted no time diving straight into great songs as the first notes of “Anonymous” rang out. Followed by “Return to Ithaka,” “Dope Nose,” and “Hash Pipe. Rivers Cuomo was in top form, effortlessly hitting every note while shredding on his guitar. Fans screamed along to every song, from the quirky “Buddy Holly” to the emotional “Say It Ain’t So,” reliving the magic of the iconic Blue album that was played full from start to finish. The band’s tight performance was a testament to why they’ve remained rock legends for decades.

The stage transported the audience to a “blue planet” with large, floating planets and rocks on the sides, giving the show a cosmic feel that matched Weezer’s iconic sound. The visuals on the large screen behind the stage made their performance an incredible trip through their music.

_**It’s a small step for Weezer, but one giant lead to Weezerkind!**_ Rivers said, while planting the Weezer Flag on the blue planet surface.

Cuomo’s playful energy had the crowd smiling from ear to ear as he delivered classic riffs and heartfelt vocals.When “Buddy Holly” kicked in, the entire venue exploded, but with “Undone – The Sweater Song” started, the entire venue sang in unison, creating a powerful moment of connection between band and fans. It was a night of pure nostalgia and joy, with Weezer proving that their _Blue Album_ is as timeless and beloved as ever. The night ended on a high note with the crowd begging for more, a testament to the unforgettable energy Weezer brought to Austin.

![Image 12: The rock band performing in matching black jumpsuits with patches, playing guitars on a smoky stage, featuring projections of asteroids and starburst lights, and white rocks in the background](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza0.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 13: Rivers Cuomo is center stage playing guitar in an astronaut outfit](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza9.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 14: Les Claypool performs live on stage, singing into a microphone while playing a double-necked transparent bass guitar, wearing a black jumpsuit with space-themed patches](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza1.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 15: The person standing on a stage playing an electric guitar](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza10.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 16: Weezer drummer Patrick Wilson is seen performing at a concert, surrounded by his blue drum kit](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza2.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 17: A crowd of people are cheering and recording at a concert, with a child in the front wearing an astronaut helmet](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza7.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 18: Rivers Cuomo is playing an electric guitar in a live concert](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza13.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 19: Weezer performs onstage with a retro-futuristic set including a stage modeled after a moon surface and a space-themed backdrop](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza4.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 20: Man in a jumpsuit and aviator sunglasses playing a gold-colored electric guitar on a stage filled with fog](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza6.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 21: Les Claypool, the American musician, wearing glasses and an astronaut-like overall, playing an electric bass guitar](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza11.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 22: Drummer playing a blue glitter drum set at a concert](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza12.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

![Image 23: Rivers Cuomo with black-rimmed glasses, playing his teal guitar that has stickers on it](https://www.theheartsounds.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Photo-Nacho-DelaGarza3.jpg)

Weezer - Photo: Nacho DelaGarza

This was a night that Austin fans won’t soon forget. From Dinosaur Jr.’s gritty, distortion-filled set to The Flaming Lips’ mind-bending psychedelic experience, to Weezer’s flawless performance of the _Blue Album_, the evening was a celebration of rock history and timeless music.

Each band brought their unique flavor to the stage, creating a perfect blend of sound and energy. The mix of nostalgia and pure rock power made this show one for the ages—an unforgettable night of music that will be talked about for years to come.

13.title: The Flaming Lips to Release Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots Blu-Ray Edition on November 1, 2024
13.content:
[![Image 1: download (1)](https://www.thatericalper.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/download-1-7.jpg)](https://www.thatericalper.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/download-1-7.jpg)

Immersing listeners deeper into a living and breathing otherworld, GRAMMY Award-winning alternative luminaries The Flaming Lips will unveil Yoshimi Battles The Pink Robots (Blu-Ray Edition) on November 1, 2024. The Atmos mixes of Yoshimi Battles The Pink Robots as well as 2020’s American Head, are available to stream now on participating digital platforms.

This marks the first release of Yoshimi Battles The Pink Robots on Blu-Ray in Dolby ATMOS mixed by Dave Fridmann & Atmos engineering & mastering by Jon Fridmann, DTS-HD 5.1 Mix mixed by Dave Fridmann & Elliot Scheiner, and DTS-HD 2.0 Hi-Res Stereo mixes by Dave Fridmann. The package insert also includes an excerpt from an interview by Wayne Coyne with Jon and Dave Fridmann, discussing the Atmos mixing and listening experience.

The Blu-Ray also notably boasts animated visualizer “Bleep Blops” and four newly remastered music videos—“Fight Test,” “Yoshimi Battles The Pink Robots Pt. 1,” Are You A Hypnotist??,” and both versions of “Do You Realize??” All music videos will also be upgraded on digital platforms, with “Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots Pt. 1” & “Fight Test” available to watch in HD leading up to release.

The Flaming Lips initially unveiled Yoshimi Battles The Pink Robots on July 16, 2002. It went on to emerge as their “biggest-selling album so far” and earn a Gold certification from the RIAA. Indicative of the record’s impact, the epic closer “Approaching Pavonis Mons by Balloon (Utopia Planitia)” garnered a GRAMMY® Award in the category of “Best Rock Instrumental Performance.” 22 years later since its arrival, signature classics such as “Ego Tripping at the Gates of Hell” and “Do You Realize??” remain staples in concert and on streaming platforms.

American Head was produced, as always, by longtime collaborator Dave Fridmann and The Lips and is comprised of thirteen cinematic tracks. Among them, “God and the Policeman,” featuring backing vocals from country superstar Kacey Musgraves.

The band is currently on the Voyage to a Blue Planet Tour with Weezer across the US through October 12, 2024. They will then pick back up with continued dates performing Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots in its entirety in Australia, the UK, Europe & Asia in 2025.

Formed in Oklahoma City, OK in 1983, The Flaming Lips have since become one of the most iconic, influential, unpredictable, and vital forces in American alternative rock music. The band has garnered three GRAMMY Awards, a Tony nomination, and an RIAA Gold-certified Record for Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots. Q Magazine named them one of the “50 Bands to See Before You Die.” The band has made countless late-night television appearances, appeared in a Super Bowl commercial, contributed to many film soundtracks, and collaborated with artists such as Miley Cyrus, Coldplay’s Chris Martin, Kacey Musgraves, Yoko Ono, The Chemical Brothers, and many more. Most recently, The LIPS have recorded an album of Nick Cave covers featuring vocalist Nell Smith called “Where The Viaduct Blooms.” They have set countless records, broken attendance records, have a hometown street named in their honor, created spectacular interactive audio/visual events now regarded as legendary. Frontman Wayne Coyne has been recognized for works of art that graced many LIPS album covers along with his traveling art exhibit (and subsequent album) “The King’s Mouth,” an audiovisual art installation that has been featured in many contemporary art museums around the US. Their latest LP, American Head, marks a return to a more melodic and song-oriented body of work and has critically been lauded as their best work in years, placing on several “Year End/Best Of lists” around the world. Even after a combination of 23 studio recordings, 16 singles, 11 compilations, 12 EPs and 11 self-released experimental collaborative oddities released in various forms,quantities and unique mediums, The Flaming Lips remain in a creative apex that has no bounds. To that end, they have become an American Treasure and created a genre all to themselves.

 Sir David Attenborough narrates this critically acclaimed series that dives deep into the marine environment of Planet Earth. Although two-thirds of the world's surface is covered with water, scientists know less about the oceans than they do about the surface of the moon. This limited series travels from various coasts to the poles to examine watery denizens ranging from the gigantic blue whale to microscopic coral polyps.

17.title: See Dominic Fike join Weezer onstage to play Say It Ain’t So
17.content:
Not for the first time in their respective careers, [Weezer](https://www.kerrang.com/artists/weezer/)’s path has just crossed with superstar actor and musician [Dominic Fike](https://www.kerrang.com/artists/dominic-fike/).

This latest meeting happened on March 15 at the 500-capacity Lodge Room in Los Angeles, where Rivers Cuomo and co. were playing a tiny show to celebrate the announcement of [The Voyage To The Blue Planet Tour](https://www.kerrang.com/weezer-announce-blue-album-anniversary-u-s-tour).

And while performing their classic Blue Album in full, they brought Dominic out onstage to sing and play guitar to Say It Ain’t So, making the occasion even more special than it already was.

Of course, Weezer will be playing the record in full a whole bunch more throughout 2024, with their upcoming tour in celebration of the LP kicking off at the Xcel Energy Center in St Paul, MN on September 4, and finishing up at the Intuit Dome in Inglewood, CA on October 11.

They’ll be joined by The Flaming Lips and Dinosaur Jr. for the whole thing, and have confirmed that they’ll also be playing “other fan favourites, rarities and more”, on top of their debut.

Check out footage of Dominic performing with Weezer below:

See the full [setlist](https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/weezer/2024/lodge-room-los-angeles-ca-3baae098.html) from the Lodge Room:

1. My Name Is Jonas

2. No One Else

3. The World Has Turned And Left Me Here

4. Buddy Holly

5. Undone – The Sweater Song

6. Surf Wax America

7. In The Garage

8. Say It Ain't So (with Dominic Fike)

9. Holiday

10. Only In Dreams

16.title: Ticket Thursday: Win pair of tickets to Weezer’s ‘The Voyage to the Blue Planet Tour’
16.content:
Get ready, because you’re about to be feeling blue!

Listen to 98 Rock ALL DAY and embark on [The Voyage to the Blue Planet Tour](https://www.98online.com/event/weezer-at-the-anthem-on-sept-14/) as Weezer celebrates 30 years of the Blue Album with The Flaming Lips and Dinosaur Jr.

All you have to do to secure your two seats is tune in at 97.9FM, 98online.com or the 98 Rock Mobile App!

Celebrating 30 years of the “Blue Album”, the band is set to play the album in full each and every night of the tour along with all your favorite Weezer songs, rarities and more!

**About Weezer:**

Weezer is an American rock band formed in Los Angeles, CA in 1992, currently consisting of Rivers Cuomo (lead vocals, lead guitar), Patrick Wilson (drums), Brian Bell (rhythm guitar, backing vocals, keyboards), and Scott Shriner (bass, backing vocals). Weezer has sold 10 million albums in the U.S., and over 35 million records worldwide. Their catalogue has included such megahits as “Buddy Holly,” “Undone (The Sweater Song),” “Say It Ain’t So,” “El Scorcho,” “Hash Pipe,” “Island In The Sun,” “Beverly Hills,” “Pork and Beans,” and more. Weezer has won Grammys, MTV Video Music Awards, and more throughout their career. Following massively acclaimed album releases in 2016 and 2017 (Weezer [The White Album] and Pacific Daydream, respectively), and two sold out amphitheatre tours with Panic! At the Disco (in 2016) and Pixies (in 2018), Weezer released a fan-inspired cover of Toto’s “Africa.” The cover propelled the band back into the charts across the board, giving Weezer their FIFTH #1, TENTH Top 5, and SIXTEENTH Top 10 at Alternative Radio, in addition to landing Top 5 on the Hot AC chart. It has since gone Platinum. They then surprise dropped a covers album at the start of 2019 — Weezer (The Teal Album) — which has been streamed over a hundred million times since its release. In 2021, Weezer released two very different but equally Weezer albums – OK Human, an orchestral pop album meditating on technology and disconnectedness, and Van Weezer, an homage to the band’s shared metal roots growing up. OK Human’s first single, “All My Favorite Songs,” was one of the biggest rock hits of 2021, and was subsequently nominated for a Grammy for “Best Rock Song.” In 2022, the band released SZNZ, a four EP project inspired by Vivaldi’s Four Seasons, and completed the European leg of the Hella Mega tour, which sold out stadiums in America throughout the year prior.

**About The Flaming Lips**

Formed in Oklahoma City, OK in 1983, The Flaming Lips have since become one of the most iconic, influential, unpredictable, and vital forces in American alternative rock music. The band has garnered three GRAMMY® Awards, a Tony nomination, and an RIAA Gold-certified Record for**_Yoshimi Battles the Pink_****_Robots_**._Q_ Magazine named them one of the “50 Bands to See Before You Die.”

The band has made countless late night television appearances, appeared in a Super Bowl commercial, contributed to many film soundtracks, and collaborated with artists such as Miley Cyrus, Coldplay’s Chris Martin, Kacey Musgraves, Yoko Ono, The Chemical Brothers, and so many more. They have set countless records, broken records, created spectacular interactive audio/visual events now regarded as legendary.

Frontman Wayne Coyne has been recognized for works of art that graced many LIPS album covers along with his traveling art exhibit**“The King’s Mouth,”**an audiovisual art installation that has been featured in many contemporary art museums around the US. Their latest LP,**_American Head_**, marks a return to a more melodic and song-oriented body of work and has critically been lauded as their best work in years placing on several Year End/Best Of lists around the world. Evan after a combination of 22 studio recordings, 16 singles, 11 compilations, 11 EP’s and 11 self-released experimental collaborative oddities released in various forms, quantities and unique mediums, The Flaming Lips remain in a creative apex that has no bounds. To that end, they have become an American Treasure and created a genre all to themselves.

**About Dinosaur Jr.**

_Sweep It Into Space_

 Here is _Sweep It Into Space_, the fifth new studio album cut by Dinosaur Jr.. during the 13th year of their rebirth. Originally scheduled for issue in mid 2020, this record’s temporal trajectory was thwarted by the coming of the Plague. But it would take more than a mere Plague to tamp down the exquisite fury of this trio when they are fully dialed-in. And _Sweep It Into Space_ is a masterpiece of zoned dialing.

In the decades since the release of Dinosaur Jr.’s original triptych of foundational albums, it has become clear that their sound — once hailed as a sort of _almost_-tamed noise — is/was/always-has-been fully functioning pop music of a sort. The subsequent generations of bands who grew up breathing Dino’s fumes managed to tinker around with the edges of their original post-hardcore song-forms enough for listeners to realize there had _always_ been melodies at the center of everything they did. What Dinosaur Jr.. produces is nothing but a beautiful new version of the rock continuum — riff, power, beat and longing, created with an eye on the infinite future.

Recorded, as usual, at Amherst’s Biquiteen, the sessions for _Sweep It Into Space_ began in the late Autumn of 2019, following a West Coast/South East tour. The only extra musician used this time with Kurt Vile.

J Mascis says, “Kurt played little lead things, like 12 string one at the beginning of ‘I Ran Away.’ Then I ended up just mimicking a few things he’d done. I was listening to a lot of Thin Lizzy, so I was trying to get some of that dueling twin lead sound. (laughs)”

“But the recording session was pretty well finished by the time things really hit the fan. So I just ended up doing more things by myself. Like the mini digital mellotron on ‘Take It Back.’ Originally I’d thought I’d have Ken Mauri (who has done keyboard work for Dino in the past) come in and play piano. But when the Lock Down happened in March, that meant I was on my own. But it was cool.”

Indeed,_Sweep It Into Space_ is a very cool album. As is typical, Lou Barlow writes and sings two of the album’s dozen tunes and Murph’s pure-Flinstonian drumming drives the record like a go cart from Hell. Lou’s songs here are as elegant as always. “Garden” is a mid-paced ballad with genteel guitar filigree giving it a ’60 Brit feel in spots. And the album’s closer, “You Wonder,” is a strangely excellent answer to the question — “How would Blue Oyster Cult handle a country tune?”

J’s tracks flow and flower in the different directions he often follows. Some are guitar howlers, like “I Met the Stones,” with a string sound midway between Hendrix and Asheton. Some are power ballads, like “And Me,” its lyrics atomized in a manner invented by Mascis, then famously borrowed by Kurt Cobain. And there are anomalies, like “Take It Back,” which starts with a blue-beat rhythm putting one in mind of Keith Richards’ Jamaican explorations (at least for a little bit.)

But there are very few moments where you wouldn’t know you were hearing Dinosaur Jr.. in blindfolded needle drop. They have a signature sound as sure as the Stooges or Sonic Youth or Discharge ever did. They continue to expand their personal universe with _Sweep It Into Space_, without ever losing their central core.

**Voyage to the Blue Planet** was [Weezer's](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer "Weezer") headlining [2024](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=2024 "2024") North American tour, occurring from [September 4](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=September_4 "September 4") to [October 12](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=October_12 "October 12"). [The Flaming Lips](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=The_Flaming_Lips "The Flaming Lips") and [Dinosaur Jr.](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Dinosaur_Jr. "Dinosaur Jr.") were the opening acts. To celebrate the 30th anniversary of _[Weezer (The Blue Album)](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer\_(The\_Blue\_Album) "Weezer (The Blue Album)")_, the album was played in full at each show.

Overview
--------

Social media posts teasing a "voyage" were first shared on [February 14](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=February_14 "February 14"), [2024](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=2024 "2024").[[1]](https://weezerpedia.com/wiki/Voyage_to_the_Blue_Planet_Tour#cite_note-1) The tour was formally announced on [March 11](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=March_11 "March 11"), accompanied by a space-themed trailer video and website redesign. A new [Weezer Fan Club](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer_Fan_Club "Weezer Fan Club") membership bundle and a [one-off anniversary performance](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer_concert:_03/15/2024 "Weezer concert: 03/15/2024") at [Club Dump](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Club_Dump "Club Dump") were also announced. _[Weezer (The Blue Album)](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer\_(The\_Blue\_Album) "Weezer (The Blue Album)")_ was set to be performed at each show in full to celebrate the album's 30th anniversary, alongside "[other] Weezer songs, rarities, and more." [The Flaming Lips](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=The_Flaming_Lips "The Flaming Lips") and [Dinosaur Jr.](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Dinosaur_Jr. "Dinosaur Jr."), who have both performed with Weezer previously, were announced as the tour's opening bands.[[2]](https://weezerpedia.com/wiki/Voyage_to_the_Blue_Planet_Tour#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://weezerpedia.com/wiki/Voyage_to_the_Blue_Planet_Tour#cite_note-3)

On [March 14](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=March_14 "March 14"), only one day after pre-sale tickets became available to fan club members and other select groups, the [September 14](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=September_14 "September 14")[show in Washington, DC](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer_concert:_09/14/2024 "Weezer concert: 09/14/2024") sold out. In response, an [additional show](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer_concert:_09/15/2024 "Weezer concert: 09/15/2024") at the same venue on the following day was added to the tour schedule.[[4]](https://weezerpedia.com/wiki/Voyage_to_the_Blue_Planet_Tour#cite_note-4) Another [additional show in Palm Desert, California](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer_concert:_10/12/2024 "Weezer concert: 10/12/2024") on [October 12](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=October_12 "October 12") was added in June.[[5]](https://weezerpedia.com/wiki/Voyage_to_the_Blue_Planet_Tour#cite_note-5)

In August, roughly two weeks before the beginning of the tour, an unknown quantity of promotional packages were sent to random fans. These contained a musical gag card, a sticker, and an unmarked white cassette. The card was produced by Joker Greeting and plays "[Buddy Holly](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Buddy_Holly "Buddy Holly")" continuously when opened. It additionally ejects confetti when an enclosed string is pulled. The sticker features an illustration of the _[Blue Album](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer\_(The\_Blue\_Album) "Weezer (The Blue Album)")_ artwork and the text "You Just Got Weezered". The cassette, housed in a blank blue J-card, contains narration by [Rivers Cuomo](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Rivers_Cuomo "Rivers Cuomo") previewing the upcoming tour, followed by the entirety of [Weezer's third demo](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer%27s_third_demo "Weezer's third demo") (not including "[Surf Wax America](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Surf_Wax_America "Surf Wax America")").

Story
-----

A breaking news report informs the audience that the Blue Planet is dying, and that Weezer is being sent to restore it. They board the [Betsy 2.0](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Betsy_2.0 "Betsy 2.0"), a shuttle which that will take them and the audience on a dangerous voyage to save the Blue Planet. The lights brighten and shows the shuttle heading up for lift off, with fans cheering the group on. As the band plays, the big screen shows Betsy flying through space, travelling through a Weezer-themed space bar and running into the alien [Bokkus](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Bokkus "Bokkus"), who has a hatred of the group. During a trek through the _[Pinkerton](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Pinkerton "Pinkerton")_ asteroid belt, Bokkus drains Betsy's shields by hurling pies and other objects at the shuttle. The shuttle crashes, which launches [M1](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=M1 "M1") to look for parts as the band plays cuts from the titular album. After the fourth part is found, the shuttle takes off for the Blue planet.

The planet is found, but its dying and requires _the Blue Album_ to come back to life. [Rivers Cuomo](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Rivers_Cuomo "Rivers Cuomo") plants a flag adorned with the [Flying =W=](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Flying_%3DW%3D "Flying =W=") in the ground, and the band performs the entire album front-to-back. The planet is shown coming back to life, with grass, trees and buildings growing as they perform. The band lands at the Blue Rocks Amphitheater and are cheered on by the planet's native population of Weezeroids, a species which Cuomo and the crowd are members of. Bokkus finds the ampitheatre and attacks with laser cannons, only to be defeated by loud speakers and the Weezeroids' laser eyes. After the credits roll, a faux news report similar to the one at the beginning of the show plays where Cuomo states that the mission has inadvertently opened up a wormhole and altered the timeline (for example, changing Rivers' name to [Kurt](https://weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Kurt_Cobain "Kurt Cobain")), and that they need to fix it before any more damage is caused.

6.title: Weezer + The Flaming Lips in Seattle
6.description: Weezer brought their "Voyage to the Blue Planet" tour to Climate Pledge Arena last night, to "celebrate" the 30th anniversary of the Blue Album. It was a packed house, and truly an all-ages show, with lots of families bringing their kids -- and from what we could see, those kids
6.content:
Weezer brought their "Voyage to the Blue Planet" tour to Climate Pledge Arena last night, to "celebrate" the 30th anniversary of the Blue Album. It was a packed house, and truly an all-ages show, with lots of families bringing their kids -- and from what we could see, those kids knew Weezer's material pretty well. The family behind us brought their six-year-old son. We even saw one couple with a baby (with ear protectors on).

The band had a very high-tech stage, with a huge high-rez video screen behind them. The four musicians came out wearing blue astronaut suits, and "launched" into their set, as the screen showed their interstellar travel. My wife said it must've been quite the bonus to the younger audience members -- like watching a concert and a sci-fi flick together (with a bit of a video game thrown in). Just before they reached the Blue Planet, they changed out of their spacesuits; Rivers was wearing a black-and-gold _Star Trek_ uniform, with the Weezer logo replacing the Star Fleet insignia. The screen showed the surface of the Blue Planet ... and we had to laugh, naturally, when they landed at "Blue Rocks Amphitheater."

Did this stage presentation seem hokey? Well, only when the musicians spoke. Their efforts at adding their own dialogue to go with these visuals was grade-Z-movie level. Rivers has always been stiff and anxious when addressing a crowd, but Brian and Scott proved that, as actors, they're terrific musicians. But the show was a feast for the eyes and ears. Sound quality was terrific, and their setlist was very generous. No encore; between this show and Peter Hook's show, perhaps more bands are taking [Midge Ure's viewpoint](https://trouserpress.com/forum/read.php?1,55168,55168#msg-55168) to heart.

WEEZER SETLIST: 

 Anonymous 

 Dope Nose/Troublemaker 

 Hash Pipe 

 Pork and Beans 

 Beverly Hills 

 Island in the Sun 

 Burndt Jamb 

 Perfect Situation 

 Run, Raven, Run/Getchoo 

 Why Bother? 

 Pink Triangle 

 You Gave Your Love to Me Softly 

 Across the Sea 

 My Name Is Jonas 

 No One Else 

 The World Has Turned and Left Me Here 

 Buddy Holly 

 Undone (The Sweater Song) 

 Surf Wax America 

 Say It Ain't So 

 In the Garage 

 Holiday 

 Only in Dreams

* * *

The Flaming Lips preceded Weezer with a great opening set. They're "the masters of low-tech," as my wife put it, but their inflatable props were great fun, especially the huge pink robots that danced onstage to "Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots." They had a silver inflatable of the words "Fuck Yeah Seattle" that Wayne hoisted over his head, and eventually tossed out to the crowd. By the end of Weezer's set, those letters all had been separated and dispersed all over the arena. Wayne did hit upon a pet peeve of mine, exhorting the crowd too much to cheer and scream and make noise. Clearly, this is something that every rock band wants, but it's annoying to me when they "ask" a crowd to do that. And with so many great songs in their own repertoire to choose from, it's hard to see why they included a Madonna cover, of all things. Still, the set was great fun, and it's always a pleasure to see this band.

FLAMING LIPS SETLIST: 

 The Spark That Bled 

 Suddenly Everything Has Changed 

 Pompeii am Götterdämmerung 

 Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots (parts 1 and 2) 

 She Don't Use Jelly 

 The Yeah Yeah Yeah Song 

 Love Yer Brain 

 Borderline 

 Do You Realize??

* * *

Dinosaur Jr opened with a six-song set, most of which was way too noisy in the arena's acoustics. I did recognize "Start Choppin," "Freak Scene" and "Just Like Heaven." And we got a good laugh right after the third song they played, when J Mascis announced, "This next song .. is the _fourth_ song of our set!"

12.title: Weezer - Utah Concert Review
12.description: Weezer didn't schedule Utah on their Voyage to the Blue Planet Tour. So we brought Utah to Weezer. Utah Concert Review went to Colorado.
12.content:
UCR On Tour • Weezer • Voyage to the Blue Planet Tour • The Flaming Lips • Dinasaur Jr. • October 1, 2024 • Blue Arena • Loveland, Colorado

Reviewed and Photographed by Alisha Gregson

![Image 1: Musician wearing sunglasses and a space-themed t-shirt playing a glittery Explorer-style electric guitar on stage](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1810-1024x683.jpg)![Image 2: Drummer, with glasses, wearing a black long-sleeve shirt and the shirt has patches on it, is sat behind a teal drum set with clear soundproofing-like dividers](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1671-1024x683.jpg)![Image 3: Rivers Cuomo playing a green guitar, wearing black rimmed glasses and a black jumpsuit with NASA and American flag patches](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1754-683x1024.jpg)![Image 4: Sean Bonniwell, singer and bass player of the American rock band The Music Machine, performs during a concert](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1845-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

I have been a Weezer fan for as long as I can remember. When it comes to ranking my favorite bands, they come second only to The Beatles. It was actually at a Weezer concert a few years ago that I first felt the desire to become a concert photographer. Just a few months later, I covered my first show. I had no idea just how much one Weezer concert would change my life.

![Image 5: The band We Were Promised Jetpacks performs on stage in front of a full house](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2158-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

Voyage to the Blue Planet
-------------------------

![Image 6: Weezer performs on stage wearing matching black space suits adorned with NASA patches and the American flag](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1657-1024x683.jpg)![Image 7: Rivers Cuomo is playing his guitar on stage](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1644-1024x683.jpg)![Image 8: Two men standing on stage and playing guitars with light beams behind them](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1724-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

Earlier this year, Weezer announced they would be doing a tour to celebrate the 30th anniversary of their self-titled debut album, better known as “The Blue Album”. The Blue Album was released in 1994 and remains their most popular album to this day. As a huge fan, I was beyond excited by this announcement. As I eagerly scanned the list of stops on their Voyage to the Blue Planet tour, I was surprised when I didn’t see Salt Lake City on the list. Doesn’t Weezer know how much Utah loves them? Did they already forget about the Billboard? Utah Concert Review wasn’t going to let this keep us from the Blue Planet. If Weezer wasn’t going to come to us, we decided we would just have to go to them.

![Image 9: Audience raising hands making a “W” sign, in the background a blurred silhouette of the musician on stage](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2077-1024x683.jpg)![Image 10: Silhouettes of people with raised hands, some of them doing different signs, at a live concert, a blurred band and a blue flag in the background](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2224-1024x683.jpg)![Image 11: Silhouetted figures raise their hands at a concert, illuminated by blue and white lights](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5507-1024x683.jpg)![Image 12: Band performs on stage illuminated with orange lights and stage fog in front of the audience](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2120-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

UCR on Tour
-----------

![Image 13: Rivers Cuomo playing a light green electric guitar on stage, with his black space suit and sunglasses on](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1787-1024x683.jpg)![Image 14: Dave Grohl performs onstage playing a gold-colored electric guitar](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1903-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

On Tuesday, October 1st, Weezer brought their tour to Loveland, Colorado. The venue, The Blue Arena, felt very fitting for this particular tour. In 2019, I lived just a few minutes away from the Blue Arena for about a year, and although I was familiar with the venue, I never had the chance to attend a concert there. I was excited about the opportunity to travel to Colorado to cover the show. I grabbed some of my favorite people, including my kids, and we set off on a Weezer road trip.

Ironically, the last Weezer concert I attended was part of their 2023 Indie Rock Road Trip tour, and I drove less than an hour to get there. This concert would end up taking seven and a half hours each way (plus an extra hour spent at the slowest Wendy’s in Wyoming), but Weezer put on a show so good that it was worth every minute of the drive.

![Image 15: A man is seen singing into a microphone while playing a guitar on a stage with a large screen in the background](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1879-1024x683.jpg)![Image 16: Weird Al Yankovic's drummer plays a blue glitter drum set in front of a black backdrop with white stripes](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1929-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

Dinosaur Jr.
------------

![Image 17: A drummer, bald and wearing glasses, plays a drum set on a stage with pink lighting](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1041-1024x683.jpg)![Image 18: Man with long white hair and a beard wearing pink glasses, a black baseball cap, and a western-style shirt singing into a microphone and playing a guitar on stage in front of a green light](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1087-1024x683.jpg)![Image 19: Bass guitarist plays on stage with Marshall stacks in the background](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5219-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

Alt-rock band Dinosaur Jr. started the night off with a short but energetic performance. Their 30-minute set was packed with electric solos and heavy riffs. They entertained the crowd with their original hits like “Freak Scene” and “Feel the Pain” and included a cover of The Cure’s “Just Like Heaven.”Over the years Weezer and Dinosaur Jr. have been on the same bill. Especially in the earlier days. It was great to see them together again on the same lineup.

![Image 20: Man with a long white beard, wearing glasses and a hat, playing an electric guitar on stage under blue and purple lighting](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_0987-1024x683.jpg)![Image 21: Man with a beard is playing a white bass guitar while on a stage with a purple light shining on him](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1114-1024x683.jpg)![Image 22: A bald drummer with glasses is playing the drums during a concert](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1083-1024x683.jpg)![Image 23: A long-haired musician plays a sparkly white electric bass guitar on a stage bathed in blue and purple light, wearing blue jeans and bright orange socks](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5225-1024x683.jpg)![Image 24: A musician wearing a baseball cap and glasses sings into a microphone while playing guitar on a stage with blue lighting](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1017-1024x683.jpg)![Image 25: The rock band Dinosaur Jr. performs on a stage with purple stage lighting in a dark auditorium](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5230-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

The Flaming Lips
----------------

![Image 26: Musician is standing on stage with a microphone](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1178-1024x683.jpg)![Image 27: Man with long curly hair, wearing a suit, sings into a microphone with his hands raised against a black background](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1234-1024x683.jpg)![Image 28: Wayne Coyne sings on stage with one hand raised in the air](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1238-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

The Flaming Lips were up next. I was looking forward to seeing what they had in store for us. I had only seen them once before, but it was hard to imagine them as an opening band. They are known for their very theatrical, over-the-top performances, and I was hoping we would get to see some of their signature flair. I am happy to say that they did not disappoint.

![Image 29: Man with orange wavy hair, wearing a blue bandana and a Colorado flag jacket, is seen in a musical performance setting with drums, accented by blue and purple lighting](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1325-1024x683.jpg)![Image 30: Man on stage in dark green shirt playing bass guitar with white body and blue and white sticker on the body](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1360-1024x683.jpg)![Image 31: Musician performs on stage with his guitar and drums set and a keyboard behind](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1366-1024x683.jpg)![Image 32: Live performance shot of Blue October on a concert stage with two massive robot-shaped balloons, emblazoned with the words “Fuck Yeah Blue October”, on either side of the stage; lasers and lights criss-cross the stage](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1434_websize-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

While their performance was slightly scaled back from the shows they headline, they still gave their fans an authentic Flaming Lips experience. Lead Singer Wayne Coyne never sang while confined in his iconic bubble, but the band’s blow-up robots made an appearance. And although they didn’t cover the crowd in excessive amounts of confetti, they carried on their tradition with their custom balloons that read “F*** yeah Blue Arena.”

![Image 33: Performance on stage with two giant eyeball balloons, a pair of lips in front, and other musicians in the background](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1498-1024x683.jpg)![Image 34: Wayne Coyne performs on stage behind a giant, illuminated set of lips and between two large eye-ball shaped props](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1505-1024x683.jpg)![Image 35: The Flaming Lips performing live on stage with large eyeball and lip props](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1524-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

The Flaming Lips played an awesome set of 10 songs that got the crowd excited. Fans sang along with their fun songs like “She Don’t Use Jelly” and “Love Yer Brain,” and everyone in the arena started dancing along with their surprising cover of Madonna’s “Borderline.” They sounded amazing as they finished off their set with their hit song, “Do You Realize??”

![Image 36: The Flaming Lips frontman, Wayne Coyne, is seen singing into a microphone in front of a rainbow arch during a concert](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1546-1024x683.jpg)![Image 37: Three band members are performing on stage, bathed in colorful lights with lasers](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5280-1024x683.jpg)![Image 38: Concertgoers watch a band perform on stage, illuminated by colorful spotlights and laser beams, with large, inflatable figures and the words FUCK YEAH BLUE ARENA displayed](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5311-1024x683.jpg)![Image 39: The singer stands on stage with a microphone, illuminated by colorful spotlights](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5281-1024x683.jpg)![Image 40: Wayne Coyne, the lead singer of the band The Flaming Lips, performs on stage under a rainbow inflatable](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1565-1024x683.jpg)![Image 41: Man with curly hair sings on stage, wearing a dark suit and holding a microphone in his raised hand](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1333-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

![Image 42: Weezer band members stand on a stage in black jumpsuits while playing guitars during a concert](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1602-1024x683.jpg)![Image 43: Weezer performs on stage in matching black astronaut jumpsuits with various patches on the sleeves, with a large screen behind them with abstract images](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1607-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

The lights dimmed, and heavy fog filled the stage as a pre-recorded video began to play on circle screens on each side of the stage. The short clip set the plot for the night and featured Weezer in full astronaut attire appearing on the news announcing their upcoming voyage through space to reach the blue planet. The rest of the concert would follow this storyline, and it made the show fun and unique. The stage setup was impressive, and the digital backdrop displayed a large rocket that was ready for takeoff.

![Image 44: Weezer](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5371-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

After a 5-minute countdown, Weezer stepped out onto the stage in front of an energetic crowd. On other stops along their tour, Weezer would be hidden inside a spaceship and then appear in front of the crowd as it is lifted. I am guessing that the stage at the Blue Arena wasn’t large enough to accommodate all the theatrics Weezer had planned. Even without a few of the extra touches, the setup was still incredible.

![Image 45: Rivers Cuomo playing guitar on stage with a drummer in the background in front of a space ship set](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1957-1024x683.jpg)![Image 46: Rivers Cuomo of Weezer plays the guitar on stage next to a drummer and in front of a spaceship background](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1952-1024x683.jpg)![Image 47: Rivers Cuomo, the lead singer of Weezer, is seen playing the guitar at a concert while dressed in an astronaut jumpsuit](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1953-1024x683.jpg)![Image 48: Musician playing a blue electric guitar that is covered with an assortment of stickers](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1925-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

Dressed in Blue space jumpsuits, Weezer gathered in the middle of the stage before taking their places. Lead singer River Cuomo stood front and center while guitarist Brian Bell, Bass Guitarist Scott Shriner,and drummer Patrick Wilson spread out across the stage. The concert was made up of three parts: the Blue Voyage Takeoff, the Pinkerton Asteroid Belt, and the Blue Planet. Blue Voyage Takeoff featured many of the band’s hits. Their high-energy songs like “Hash Pipe,” “Beverly Hills,” and “Dope Nose” really got the crowd excited. I have always loved “Pork and Beans,” and it’s amazing hearing it performed live. “Perfect Situation” was a song I had overlooked in the past, but over the last couple of years, it has become one of my favorites. I couldn’t believe how much energy was in that arena, and we hadn’t even arrived at the Blue Planet yet.

![Image 49: Man wearing glasses and a black spacesuit, playing a bass guitar on stage during a concert, his hands showing tattoos](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1910-1024x683.jpg)![Image 50: Musician with long hair and sunglasses plays a glittery gold electric guitar on stage, with bright white lights in the background](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1902-1024x683.jpg)![Image 51: Guitarist is playing an electric guitar on stage in green light](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1982-1024x683.jpg)![Image 52: Man playing a double neck bass guitar on stage](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1697-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

After being attacked, the Weezer spaceship crash-landed in the Pinkerton Asteroid Belt. They then performed a set of 5 songs from their cult classic Pinkerton album, beginning with “Getchoo” and “Why Bother?” Next, they played “Pink Triangle” and then finished out their mini Pinkerton set with “You Gave Your Love to Me Softly” and “Across the Sea.”I was surprised that they didn’t include “El Scorcho” or “The Good Life,” but it won’t be long before Weezer does a Pinkerton tour, and they won’t have to leave anything out.

![Image 53: Musicians Rivers Cuomo and Brian Bell of Weezer performing at the Fiddler's Green Amphitheatre in Greenwood Village, Colorado on July 14, 2023](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5435-1024x683.jpg)![Image 54: Silhouetted audience members are raising their hands in the air, illuminated by bright blue stage lights](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2430_websize-683x1024.jpg)![Image 55: Rivers Cuomo of Weezer, wearing an American flag and circle badge on his black jacket, plays a Stratocaster in front of his bandmates](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5438-683x1024.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

![Image 56: The rock band Weezer performs on stage with a large video screen behind them, stage fog in the foreground](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5425-1024x683.jpg)![Image 57: Rivers Cuomo is on stage wearing black jacket with patches, playing a guitar, under blue light](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5468-1024x683.jpg)![Image 58: A man wearing glasses plays guitar on stage in front of a large screen depicting a spaceship](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5484-1024x683.jpg)![Image 59: A man on a stage wearing black glasses and a black space suit playing a blue guitar](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5485-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

The Blue Album
--------------

![Image 60: A man holds a flag with a large W on a smoke-filled stage in front of an audience](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2212_websize-1024x683.jpg)![Image 61: Weezer performing onstage in front of a blue flag with the band's logo](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2222-1024x683.jpg)![Image 62: Weezer's Rivers Cuomo performing on stage with the band's logo on a flag in the background, on a smoke-filled stage](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2213-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

The band disappeared from the stage for a brief moment while their intergalactic travels continued to unfold on the screens. The crowd could hardly contain their excitement as Weezer finally landed on the blue planet. The band reemerged on the stage, Rivers now wearing a black and yellow Star Trek-inspired outfit, only to find the blue planet wasn’t blue at all; it was gray, and it was dying. While holding a blue flag with the Weezer logo, Rivers exclaimed, “We need to play the blue album to bring it back to life!” Then, after planting the flag on the blue planet, Rivers said, “That’s one small step for Weezer, one giant leap for Weezerkind.”

![Image 63: Silhouettes of people with raised hands, some of them doing different signs, at a live concert, a blurred band and a blue flag in the background](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2224-1024x683.jpg)![Image 64: A guitarist with arms raised stands on a stage with a blue flag behind him, a crowd of people raises hands and cheers](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2226-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

The energy in the arena was insane as they kicked off the Blue Album Set with “My Name is Jonas.” Hearing the entire crowd sing along with every word was incredible. A friend recently described the Blue Album as one of the best albums ever, without a single skippable song, and it’s true: every song is a hit. Cannons of blue streamer confetti shot off, covering the fans on the floor. Weezer kept the crowd on their feet for the rest of the night as they played through the remaining songs in the same order they were on the album.

![Image 65: Rivers Cuomo is singing into a microphone while playing a custom-decorated guitar and wearing a Star Trek-like top on stage at a Weezer concert](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2303-1024x683.jpg)![Image 66: Rivers Cuomo playing a blue, green, and yellow sticker-covered Fender Stratocaster while wearing a yellow Star Trek uniform](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2309-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

Fans went wild when they played “Buddy Holly,” and I believe this was the first Weezer concert I have been to where they didn’t save that one for the very end. During the intro of “Undone – The Sweater Song,” fans enjoyed hearing Brian Bell ad-lib the intro and make Colorado-specific references. I have seen them perform this song several times now, but this was the first time I witnessed them include the intro dialogue. I always look forward to hearing my all-time favorite Weezer song, “Say It Ain’t So,” and I just love the way Rivers performs it live. By the time we were all singing along to “In the Garage,” I knew we were nearing the end, and I found myself wishing the concert could continue throughout the night.

![Image 67: Band called Weezer is performing on stage in front of a live audience](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5512-1024x683.jpg)![Image 68: A concert featuring a band playing under blue stage lights and a backdrop depicting planets and celestial bodies](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5514-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

Weezer covered the crowd once again in blue confetti and then finished off their set with “Only in Dreams.”. Having played the Blue Album in its entirety, there was no need for an encore. After putting on one of the most amazing concerts I have ever seen, they gathered once again in the middle of the stage to say goodbye to their fans.

![Image 69: Man playing a guitar on stage while wearing Star Trek uniform, with a flag in the background](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2298-1024x683.jpg)![Image 70: Rivers Cuomo plays guitar at a Weezer concert](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2325-1-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

For many reasons, this was a night I will never forget. I am not sure how anything will ever top the way I felt, watching my kids sing every word to every song on my favorite album or hearing them talk about how incredible the concert was. The kids especially loved how this concert had a story. My friend’s 4-year-old son felt amazing after Brian Bell connected with him and smiled right at him multiple times throughout the night.My 8-year-old daughter told me later that she cried during the concert because she couldn’t believe she got to see Rivers singing in person. Weezer has been my 13-year-old daughter’s favorite band for years now, and it was so sweet to see her in her own Buddy Holly-style glasses, dancing and singing.

![Image 71: Singer Rivers Cuomo performing on stage, wearing a Star Trek-inspired shirt with the Weezer logo and playing a sticker-covered guitar](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_2236-1024x683.jpg)![Image 72: Drummer with glasses performing on a blue drum kit with clear plastic shields at an outdoor venue with a starry background](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1758-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

A framed set list that a crew member gave my 11-year-old son now sits on a shelf in his room. If you have ever wondered if you should take your kids to one of their favorite bands, I highly recommend it, especially if that band is Weezer. While I had fully intended to watch the stage all night, I sometimes found it hard to keep my eyes off the kids. Seeing the way they enjoyed the concert made the experience even better. But because Weezer does deserve my full, undivided attention, I thought it was necessary to see them again (kid-free this time) at their LA show just before the tour ended.

![Image 73: A band is performing on stage with blue lighting and background scenery](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_5516-1024x683.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

Everything about the Voyage to the Blue Planet tour was so impressive. I loved every second of it, and it exceeded all my expectations. Weezer set the bar high, and with the anniversary of the Pinkerton album coming up, I can’t even imagine what they have in store for us next.

![Image 74: Concert set list of 25 songs including Anonymous, Return to Ithaka, Dope Nose, Hash Pipe, and Pork and Beans](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/IMG_4611-2-768x1024.jpg)![Image 75: Rivers Cuomo is performing on stage in a black astronaut jumpsuit, playing an electric guitar adorned with stickers](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DSC_1802-1.jpg)

[Photo Credit: Alisha Gregson](http://www.instagram.com/alishagregsonphotography)

[![Image 76: DSC_1699](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/gallery/weezer-colorado/thumbs/thumbs-DSC_1699.jpg)](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/gallery/weezer-colorado/DSC_1699.jpg)

[![Image 77: DSC_1697](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/gallery/weezer-colorado/thumbs/thumbs-DSC_1697.jpg)](https://utahconcertreview.com/wp-content/gallery/weezer-colorado/DSC_1697.jpg)

A Weezer Concert Film Is Set For Release
========================================

If you missed Weezer performing live in the area, you kind of get a second chance. A Weezer Concert Film is set for release! It’s a stop on their Voyage…
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Updated Sep 30, 2024 10:43 AM EDT

![Image 4: Weezer performing live in concert](https://wdhafm.com/uploads/2024/09/Weezer-Live.jpg?format=auto&optimize=high&width=1440)

_(Photo by Amy Sussman/Getty Images for The Recording Academy_

Share this story

If you missed Weezer performing live in the area, you kind of get a second chance. A Weezer Concert Film is set for release! It’s a stop on their Voyage To The Blue Planet Tour. Now, I reviewed the show I went to, but I have to reiterate a few things.

First off, yes, [Weezer](https://weezer.com/) plays the Blue Album (their debut) in its entirety. And they knock it out of the park. The guitar riffs, the harmonies, the slow build-ups. It’s a sight to behold. They also play a ton of fan favorites before getting into the Blue Album.

About The Weezer Concert Film
-----------------------------

Now, since you have a chance to see this concert streaming from your own home, I don’t want to ruin much. I’ll just tell you that there’s a really cool story that takes place throughout the show. Rivers Cuomo and the band head out on a space adventure. Let’s just say that throughout it, they go through other planets and galaxies and that’s where the “Other” songs come into play.

The concert footage was filmed at Boston’s TD Garden on September 10 th. They’ve made it into a full-fledged concert film which you can stream either October 13 th or October 14 th. The tour’s not over yet, but I think this is so cool for fans who passed on tickets but ae kicking themselves for not going. I almost didn’t. My wife and I thought it was pretty expensive and it was tough to get seats.[But after witnessing the whole show, I can tell you…..it was worth it](https://wdhafm.com/2024/09/16/weezers-30th-anniversary/)!

I think even from home you’ll get a great experience and be able to follow the story. Plus, the sound will most likely be better as I’m sure it will come from the mixing board.

Even if you’re a passive Weezer fan I highly recommend this. It’s a really fun experience!

It’s A Linkin Park Special Event On YouTube This Thursday
---------------------------------------------------------

We saw the[**Linkin Park countdown**](https://wdhafm.com/2024/08/26/linkin-park-timer-counting-down/) and then counted up. And now we are waiting for a Linkin Park special event on YouTube This Thursday.

The event will take place at 6pm EST on Youtube Thursday. More waiting , I know, but at least we know something is definitely coming. Or at least we think!

I was hoping that Linkin Park would be announcing either a tour with rotating vocalists or maybe even an album of new music starring guest vocalists throughout the album. I thought that would be something really fun and not take away from Chester Bennington’s legacy.

A tour would be fun to see the rest of the band. They are super talented and play so well live. I thought it’d be cool to have a tour with revolving singers at different locations or something like that.[An album of new music](https://wdhafm.com/listicle/new-music-releases-to-be-excited-for/) would be tremendous as well, however instead of announcing one new singer, I thought they could just have different guests on each track.

What makes [Linkin Park](https://xn--pda.linkinpark.com/) so special is their ability to craft songs that are all over the map sound and no two songs sound alike. There’s always a unique spin and they could go from ballad to in-your-face, loud, and heavy guitars in a matter of minutes. But of course, to me, the band was and always will be Chester Bennington. His voice was so extraordinary. He went from melodic, soft singing to near screams in just seconds. And live, he always sounded flawless.

The Linkin Park sound couldn’t be defined. It had elements of hip hop sure, but it was straight-up hard rock at moments - trippy, experimental tribal anthem the next. You really got a good mix that was so interesting!

BREAKING THE HABIT
------------------

What a cool, interesting vibe. It's got a lot going on in this tune, with some cool drums and a relatable lyrical theme from Chester. Really cool stuff!

MY DECEMBER
-----------

Such a dark sounding song. Yet it's hopeful and intriguing, and emotional all at once. A real masetrpiece.

WAITING FOR THE END
-------------------

This one pumps me up. From the album that left fans divided "A Thousand Suns". There's no denying that this song is filled with hope and passion in Chester's voice.

LIES GREED MISERY
-----------------

This is really a rare example of hip hop - metal. It's got elements from both genres and is so angst ridden, that it fuels and pumps you up. Such great screams towards the end!

SHADOW OF THE DAY
-----------------

A really nice ballad that just has a lot of heart and emotion. Really a cool laid back vibe with a nice melodic hook!
